propositions: The reconciler core currently reaches directly into Jira adapter modules without a named abstraction; this story introduces a Backend facade with five role Protocols (TicketTransport, OutboundMapper, InboundMapper, FieldSanitizer, IdentityConvention) and three optional capability Protocols detected via isinstance checks.
JiraBackend is implemented as a thin delegation shim wrapping existing Jira modules (AcliClient, field mappers, sanitizers) with zero behavior change and no core call-site rewiring.

IdentityConvention is a new pure convention object that encapsulates the rebar-id label format (reading and writing RemoteRef identity), currently hand-inlined across four core modules but not rewired here.

A backend-agnostic contract test suite parameterized over JiraBackend (with injected mock transport) and FakeBackend validates outbound-to-inbound round-trips, sanitizer idempotence, capability dispatch, and RemoteRef stamping/parsing.
Characterization tests verify pure Jira mapper outputs (outbound_fields, inbound extraction, adf.fit_text_to_adf_limit) match byte-for-byte with current main behavior.
No core differ, apply, applier, or other reconciler call-site modules are modified; only new _backend.py, adapters/jira/backend.py, adapters/jira/identity.py, and test files are added.
